title: Webex Contact Center Customer Wait Time SLA by Skill Group
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Webex Contact Center Customer Wait Time SLA by Skill Group' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_webex_contact_center_customer_wait_time_sla_by_s` (UC-11.3.44), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — Webex Contact Center Customer Wait Time SLA by Skill Group", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=contact_center` sourcetype='wxcc:call_legs' that satisfy the UC-11.3.44 SPL filters for 'Webex Contact Center Customer Wait Time SLA by Skill Group'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `contact_center` / `wxcc:call_legs` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-11.3.44.

dataSources: `sourcetype=wxcc:queue_stats` (custom via API), `sourcetype=wxcc:call_legs` Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Webex Contact Center GraphQL API via HEC, `Cisco Webex Add-on` (Splunkbase #5781) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=contact_center sourcetype="wxcc:call_legs" queue_name=*
| eval answered_in_sla=if(queue_wait_sec<=30 AND isnotnull(agent_id), 1, 0)
| eval answered=if(isnotnull(agent_id), 1, 0)
| eval abandoned=if(isnull(agent_id) AND disposition=="Abandoned", 1, 0)
| bin _time span=30m
| stats count as offered, sum(answered) as answered, sum(answered_in_sla) as in_sla, sum(abandoned) as abandoned, avg(queue_wait_sec) as avg_wait, perc95(queue_wait_sec) as p95_wait by _time, queue_name, skill_group
| eval sla_pct=round(in_sla*100/offered, 1)
| eval abandon_pct=round(abandoned*100/offered, 1)
| table _time, queue_name, skill_group, offered, answered, in_sla, sla_pct, abandoned, abandon_pct, avg_wait, p95_wait
| sort _time, -offered
description: Queue-level SLA metrics hide performance disparities across skill groups. A blended 80% service level may mask that billing support hits 95% while technical support languishes at 55%. Granular skill-group SLA tracking exposes which specializations need staffing adjustments, schedule optimization, or skills-based routing tuning — directly preventing customer churn in the skill groups that matter most to revenue.
value: Early 'Webex Contact Center Customer Wait Time SLA by Skill Group' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Ingest WxCC queue and call leg data. Define SLA threshold per skill group (commonly 80% of calls answered within 30 seconds, but varies: sales may target 20 seconds, tier-2 support may allow 60 seconds). Build a `skill_group_sla_target` lookup with per-group thresholds. Compare actual performance against target every 30 minutes. Alert when any skill group drops below its SLA target for 2 consecutive periods. Track p95 wait time as a customer experience indicator — even if average wait is acceptable, long tail waits destroy satisfaction. Provide real-time wallboard data and daily reports for workforce managers. Correlate with agent state data (UC-11.3.42) to determine if poor SLA is caused by insufficient staffing or high NotReady time.
visualization: Table (skill groups with SLA status — green/red), Gauge (SLA % per skill group), Line chart (SLA trend per skill group over 30 days), Bar chart (p95 wait time by skill group).
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; primary SPL uses raw or vendor-normalized event fields.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Webex Contact Center GraphQL API via HEC, `Cisco Webex Add-on` (Splunkbase #5781).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=wxcc:queue_stats` (custom via API), `sourcetype=wxcc:call_legs`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest WxCC queue and call leg data. Define SLA threshold per skill group (commonly 80% of calls answered within 30 seconds, but varies: sales may target 20 seconds, tier-2 support may allow 60 seconds). Build a `skill_group_sla_target` lookup with per-group thresholds. Compare actual performance against target every 30 minutes. Alert when any skill group drops below its SLA target for 2 consecutive periods. Track p95 wait time as a customer experience indicator — even if average wait is accepta…

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=contact_center sourcetype="wxcc:call_legs" queue_name=*
| eval answered_in_sla=if(queue_wait_sec<=30 AND isnotnull(agent_id), 1, 0)
| eval answered=if(isnotnull(agent_id), 1, 0)
| eval abandoned=if(isnull(agent_id) AND disposition=="Abandoned", 1, 0)
| bin _time span=30m
| stats count as offered, sum(answered) as answered, sum(answered_in_sla) as in_sla, sum(abandoned) as abandoned, avg(queue_wait_sec) as avg_wait, perc95(queue_wait_sec) as p95_wait by _time, queue_name, skill_group
| eval sla_pct=round(in_sla*100/offered, 1)
| eval abandon_pct=round(abandoned*100/offered, 1)
| table _time, queue_name, skill_group, offered, answered, in_sla, sla_pct, abandoned, abandon_pct, avg_wait, p95_wait
| sort _time, -offered
```

Understanding this SPL

**Webex Contact Center Customer Wait Time SLA by Skill Group** — Queue-level SLA metrics hide performance disparities across skill groups. A blended 80% service level may mask that billing support hits 95% while technical support languishes at 55%. Granular skill-group SLA tracking exposes which specializations need staffing adjustments, schedule optimization, or skills-based routing tuning — directly preventing customer churn in the skill groups that matter most to revenue.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=wxcc:queue_stats` (custom via API), `sourcetype=wxcc:call_legs`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Webex Contact Center GraphQL API via HEC, `Cisco Webex Add-on` (Splunkbase #5781). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: contact_center; **sourcetype**: wxcc:call_legs. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=contact_center, sourcetype="wxcc:call_legs". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **answered_in_sla** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.

• `eval` defines or adjusts **abandoned** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by _time, queue_name, skill_group** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **sla_pct** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **abandon_pct** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.

• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.


Step 3 — Validate
Compare with Cisco Webex Control Hub analytics, audit, and service status for the same time range.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table (skill groups with SLA status — green/red), Gauge (SLA % per skill group), Line chart (SLA trend per skill group over 30 days), Bar chart (p95 wait time by skill group).
